title: Review: mime-tree typed header API (5ca80b0..HEAD)
notes:
API contract risk: MEDIUM — pre-1.0 crate (0.3.0) with substantive but addressable contract gaps; the worst items (missing #[non_exhaustive] on 3 public structs, mail-parser representation locked into HeaderDateTime, URL form behavior defined by an address parser, Raw form silently drops non-UTF-8) are fixable without breaking working callers if addressed before 1.0.
API contract confidence: 75% chance no missed issue. Least confident flags: MIME-o2c.5 (Copy derive — depends on whether maintainer ever wants non-Copy fields), MIME-o2c.13 (sum-type match — could be framed as ergonomics rather than contract), MIME-o2c.17 (more doc examples — polish). Uncertainty driven by: did not probe mail-parser 0.11 internals to confirm exact delegation behavior; did not run to_rfc3339/to_timestamp with deliberately invalid HeaderDateTime values to capture actual output; did not survey downstream callers in ~/GIT or ~/WORK to see if any already depend on the current serde wire format.
bd-review-loop: iter=1 verdict=question_tool_invoked failures=1 history=; 
API contract risk (iter 2): MEDIUM — iter 1 already cleared the obvious wins; iter 2 added 7 findings, of which MIME-o2c.28 (asText form missing — RFC 8621 §4.1.2.2 not implemented despite the API claiming to expose 'the RFC 8621 As* forms') is the only one that materially worsens the verdict. The remaining iter 2 findings (derived Eq semantics .24/.25, HeaderForm Copy .26, missing JMAP-token converter .27, missing ParsedHeader composition .29, empty-result ambiguity .30) are evolutions of issues already flagged in iter 1 or non-blocking shape concerns. Net: contract is workable today, has visible JMAP-completeness gap (missing Text form), and accumulated 14+7=21 api-contract findings — too many for a stable 1.0 release as-is, appropriate count for a 0.3.x iterating surface.
API contract confidence (iter 2): 30% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) MIME-o2c.27 — whether downstream JMAP servers actually want a from_str on HeaderForm or are happy hand-rolling; (b) MIME-o2c.29 — whether the explicit non-composition is a deliberate layering choice (mime-tree exposes byte ranges, callers compose) rather than a gap. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no review of part.rs/message.rs/parse.rs to confirm what ParsedHeader actually contains and whether a composition helper would be straightforward; (2) no review of how downstream JMAP server crates (none yet exist for this workspace) currently consume the API; (3) Cargo.toml has no doctest features or doc-rs configuration audited; (4) did not run cargo public-api / cargo semver-checks to look for hidden surface (e.g. impl traits, type aliases). Bikeshedding signal: noticeable. Remaining gaps after iter 2 are increasingly opinion-flavoured. Iter 3 unlikely to find anything beyond P3-opinion territory.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — the typed header module is small and reads cleanly; idiom gaps are concentrated in the public type-derive set (missing Hash, missing Default, From-as-free-fn, bool-instead-of-enum for tz_sign) rather than in control flow or borrow handling. No unsafe, no panics in production paths, no macros. Most idiom-relevant control-flow issues (unreachable! arm, awkward split_last, duplicated trim closures) are already filed by the contract pass.
Rust idiom confidence: 80% chance no missed issue. Least confident flags: MIME-o2c.33 (asymmetric borrow on Copy type — real but tiny, marked opinion), MIME-o2c.36 (Default derive — taste-flavoured, marked opinion). Uncertainty driven by: (1) did not check mail_parser::DateTime's actual derive list to confirm it is in fact Copy (assumed from its all-primitive fields); (2) did not survey downstream consumer crates to confirm Hash/Default would actually be reached for (argued from generic JMAP-server design intuition rather than observed call sites); (3) did not run cargo clippy --pedantic to see if it catches any of the same idioms automatically. Bikeshedding signal: high. Iter 1 of the contract pass already collected the structural complaints (unreachable, split_last, duplicated closures, Copy derives, missing non_exhaustive, missing Display); this pass is largely derive-list and conversion-style tightening. Further iteration would almost certainly produce only opinion-tier findings.
